A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same trajectory-control image-editing work. All 18 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across four editing tasks, a 42-participant user study, hyperparameter analyses, and additional StableDiffusion 3 results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds computational-budget comparisons and further qualitative robustness results.

M1.justification: The trajectory-control objective, adjoint computation, control updates, and trajectory simulation remain unchanged. Algorithm 3 makes the existing backward timestep loop explicit. Zeroth-order gradients and reward-aware initialization are proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use REFL-prompt images, Pick-a-Pic, ImageNet-1k, and CelebA-HQ for the same four editing tasks. Additional robustness tests and example images retain this coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Gradient Ascent, inversion+DPS, inversion+FreeDoM, and inversion+TFG. The guidance-tradeoff comparison retains DPS, FreeDoM, and TFG. Newly discussed RF-Solver, FireFlow, and FlowChef are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 6 revises the proposed method's iterations from 25 to 20 for StableDiffusion 1.5 and 15 for StableDiffusion 3, and changes SD3 human-preference TFG settings from (rho, mu)=(1,5) to (5,1). Appendix A.2 replaces the identification of inversion depth with T by a sampling-step fraction; SD3 depth 0.7 now corresponds to T approximately 0.15 instead of the previously stated T=0.7. Figure 4(b) adds comparisons across computational budgets. These reported revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds performance-versus-FLOPs comparisons addressing computational-budget confounding and qualitative guidance-strength sweeps examining degradation (Figures 4(b) and 7). It expands the existing depth/iteration ablation from N={1,20} to N={1,10,15,20} in Figure 6. The earlier initialization-strategy analysis is retained as Figure 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. User-study reporting remains unchanged; revised optimization-iteration counts are not repeated-run statistics.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and 7 retain their numerical results, but Figure 4(b) adds findings of better reward and fidelity at comparable FLOPs, and Figures 6, 7, and 9 add or replace qualitative outcomes. Table 8 updates all timings: for SD1.5, Ours changes from 59.60 to 60.63 seconds and TFG from 32.74 to 37.26 seconds. It also adds FLOP counts, including 590.93 TFLOPs/image for Ours on SD1.5. Revised settings prevent interpreting these timings as same-setting efficiency gains.

T1.justification: The optimal-control formulation, PMP conditions, Proposition 1, and its proof remain unchanged. Replacing sigma with eta in Equation 1 clarifies noise notation already distinguished in Appendix A.1; it introduces no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free trajectory optimization, applicability to diffusion and flow-matching models, and reward–fidelity performance without reward hacking.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new computational-budget results as evidence that additional computation alone does not explain its advantage, and expands discussion of guidance robustness and iteration convergence. The limitations discussion changes the stated runtime overhead from about 80% to 40–60%, argues that performance justifies the cost, and adds possible zeroth-order guidance and reward-aware initialization extensions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly specifies 50/28 sampling steps and 512×512/768×768 resolutions for SD1.5/SD3, and explains the scheduler-dependent inversion-depth mapping. Table 8 newly identifies human-preference settings with ImageReward as its profiling setup. These disclosures improve implementation specificity without establishing changes to previously unspecified resolutions or sampling-step counts.

R1.justification: New Appendix C provides a focused comparison with RF-Solver/RF-Edit, FireFlow, and FlowChef, distinguishing whole-trajectory reward optimization from solver improvements, attention reuse, and stepwise guidance. Free2Guide is additionally cited for prospective zeroth-order gradients. The main related-work sections and overall research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section ordering remain unchanged. Local discussion and hyperparameter explanations are expanded, appendix organization is extended, and conference headers, acknowledgments, and an LLM-use disclosure are added.

P2.justification: Figure 4 gains computational-cost plots; its former initialization panel becomes Figure 5 with a redrawn noise-schedule plot. The iteration-ablation grid is enlarged, and new Figures 7 and 9 provide guidance sweeps and an example gallery. Table 8 gains FLOP rows, while existing tables receive spacing and color refinements. This substantially expands the visual presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The computational-budget comparison, expanded robustness evidence, and clearer sampler specifications improve comparison fairness and reproducibility. The gain is limited by unexplained setting revisions alongside unchanged benchmark scores, which leave their correspondence unresolved. The timing updates therefore do not independently establish improved efficiency.
